cards.subject: a bright playful Montessori bedroom for a child aged 2 to 5, with a low birch toddler daybed and a crocheted play mat
cards.scene: A bright airy room with a pale ash plank floor. A rectangular sand crocheted play mat lies on the floor with a few vintage wooden toys on it: a stacking ring tower, a small wooden train and painted blocks. On the RIGHT side wall, away from the mural: a low birch toddler daybed, 140 by 70 cm and 35 cm high, with checkered and striped cotton bolster pillows in sand and oat, beside it an open birch shelf 60 cm high with three picture books facing front, and one small framed botanical print at child eye level. Crisp morning daylight from a window on the RIGHT falls in clear bright patches on the floor. A toddler girl of about two and a half in a blush knit sweater and cream trousers sits on the rug in the middle of the floor with her back to the camera, holding a crocheted play mat on the floor with a few vintage-style wooden toys on it, her face turned away from the camera so no facial detail is visible, well away from the mural. Palette: oat, pale birch, warm cream, muted sage and white.
cards.framing: Shot from the left part of the room at eye level, turned about 25 degrees toward the mural wall, so the RIGHT side wall is in view. The frame shows a floor-to-ceiling section of the mural wall around the big pink and yellow cosmos flowers of the meadow and the butterflies above them: the ceiling line at the top of the frame, the skirting board and a strip of floor at the bottom; the mural continues beyond the frame edges at its true scale.

cards.subject: a warm playful Fun Haus bedroom for a child aged 6 to 10, with a low linen-cushioned daybed and an arch-front shelf
cards.scene: A golden room with a dark walnut herringbone floor. A flat-weave wool rug in caramel and cream stripes lies on the floor, with a round cool blue pouf and a pill-shaped cream cushion on it. On the LEFT side wall, away from the mural: a low cream Oliver daybed, 90 by 200 cm, with natural linen cushions, a caramel-and-cream striped bolster and a small barberry cushion, beside it a low cream arch-front shelf 70 cm high with chapter books and a wooden pencil cup, and a small framed vintage circus print above. Warm golden hour sunlight from a window on the LEFT stretches in long amber patches across the floor. A sheer cream linen curtain hangs at the extreme right edge of the frame, close to the camera and slightly out of focus, as a foreground layer. Palette: cream, caramel, brick and cool blue.
cards.framing: Shot from the right part of the room at natural eye level, turned about 30 degrees toward the mural wall, so the LEFT side wall is in view. The frame shows a floor-to-ceiling section of the mural wall around the big pink and yellow cosmos flowers of the meadow and the butterflies above them: the ceiling line at the top of the frame, the skirting board and a strip of floor at the bottom; the mural continues beyond the frame edges at its true scale. Nothing stands in front of the mural.

clips.motion: The camera stays completely still on a tripod and does not move at all. A toddler girl of about two and a half in a blush knit sweater and cream trousers sits on the rug with her back to the camera and slowly plays with a crocheted play mat on the floor with a few vintage-style wooden toys on it, moving it along the rug and then picking up the next toy. Her face is never visible to the camera, not even in profile: only the back of her head, her hair and her clothes are seen. She stays on the rug, far from the big pink and yellow cosmos flowers of the meadow and the butterflies above them, and never passes in front of the mural. The warm light stays constant.

clips.motion: A smooth slow first-person walk-in: the camera advances steadily straight forward into the room at natural eye level, as if a person is slowly entering, with no sideways drift, no tilt and no rotation. The sheer cream curtain in the extreme foreground on the right leaves the frame as the camera advances past it, and the nearer objects shift more than the farther ones, giving a natural depth parallax.
